signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Strait of Hormuz Escalation
signals.text: CHF gained +1.189% (n=6) as the G10 leader while AUD slid -2.194% (n=4) as laggard to post a 3.383% bilateral spread, driving AUD/CHF to close Friday at 0.5631. Weekend Iranian naval strikes on two tankers near the Strait of Hormuz accelerate defensive safe-haven demand into CHF while penalizing high-beta commodity currencies, overriding AUD's +485bp policy carry advantage. The Sydney/Tokyo open tests liquidity beneath the 0.5627 multi-session support. Trade bias: Short AUD/CHF into the open; haven flows overpower the positive carry spread. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open following weekend Strait of Hormuz naval escalation. Risk: Immediate geopolitical de-escalation headlines triggering short covering back toward 0.5753 fair value.
evidence: Two oil tankers struck mines near Strait of Hormuz

signals.title: USD/CAD — Employment Divergence + Crowded Short Positioning
signals.text: CAD COT LF net short stands at -85,289 contracts (18.5% long) as USD/CAD closed Friday at 1.4128 following sharp North American macro divergence. October US non-farm payrolls surged +165k versus +65k expected while Canadian employment shed 4.7k, reinforcing the +140bp SOIS carry advantage favoring the dollar. The Sydney/Tokyo open sets up continuation toward fresh highs above 1.4150. Trade bias: Long USD/CAD into the open; divergence in labor fundamentals sustains the rally against crowded shorts. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open confirming post-NFP dollar follow-through. Risk: Reversal in crude prices dampening CAD selling and pushing spot back under the 1.4069 SMA20.
evidence: SOFR vs CORRA carry +140bp in USD favor

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded COT Short Overhang + Yield Disadvantage
signals.text: EUR COT LF short sits at an extreme -104,030 contracts (31.8% long, 52-week percentile 2, z=-1.80) as EUR/USD closed Friday at 1.1143 below all key daily moving averages. Resilient US payrolls support the Fed's restrictive stance, maintaining a +148bp SOIS carry buffer in favor of the dollar against €STR. Monday's Euro Area Eurogroup meeting and German trade data determine if technical support holds. Trade bias: Short EUR/USD into the open; rate differentials favor USD continuation despite crowded short exposure. Catalyst: Euro Area Eurogroup Meeting at 00:00 UTC followed by German Trade Balance. Risk: Hawkish Eurogroup commentary or upside German trade surplus triggering an unwind toward the 1.1195 SMA20.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Wedge vs Options Downside Hedging
signals.text: USD/JPY closed Friday at 158.43, underpinned by a +269bp SOFR-TONA carry advantage, even as 25-delta risk reversals trade at an extreme -1.97 put skew. Leveraged funds hold a net short JPY position of -21,213 contracts (92nd percentile), meaning further spot pullbacks risk disorderly position unwinds. Weekend geopolitical tension tests whether safe-haven yen demand overwhelms the yield deficit. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY above 158.00; wide carry spread anchors dip-buying interest. Catalyst: Sydney/Tokyo open price action against Friday's 158.47 resistance zone. Risk: Geopolitical escalation sparking severe risk-off unwinds that push spot through the 157.30 SMA50.
